# Plugging a third-party executor into a deployment

An executor implements the unary `Execute` verb plus the executor-observability
handshake. The deployment learns everything else from the handshake: the
executor's attribute schema, its error classes and its tags all govern what
template authors may write and how the graph routes.

## Name the endpoint

The deployment's only knowledge of the executor is one entry:

```yaml
persistence:
  driver: sqlite
  sqlite:
    path: /var/lib/rimsky/state.db
claim_producers: {}
named_locks: {}
executors:
  "third-party":
    transport: grpc
    endpoint: "peer:9400"
    protocols: ["executor"]
```

## The advertisement reaches the deployment

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/executors/third-party"
```

The entry reports `reachability_status: reachable` and carries the executor's
whole advertisement: its declared error classes
(`third-party/broken`, `third-party/refused`), its declared tags
(`third-party.refused`, `third-party.served`), and its expected-attributes
schema.

## Templates are held to that schema

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/templates/validate" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$SPEC"
```

Four things are checked against the advertisement.

A property whose type contradicts the executor's is rejected — "the executor is
authoritative on types":

```yaml
nodes:
  - type: w
    executor: third-party
    attributes:
      schema: {type: object, properties: {echo: {type: integer}}}
```

A property the executor's closed schema does not declare is rejected as "not
declared in executor's expected_attributes_schema".

An `error_types` entry naming a class outside the executor's vocabulary comes
back as a warning — "is not in any declared vocabulary".

A subscription filtering on a tag the executor never declared is rejected, and
the refusal names the sending node and its executor — "is not declared by
sender".

## A template written to the advertisement

```yaml
name: execproto
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: okworker
    executor: third-party
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          outcome: {type: string, default: ok}
          echo:    {type: string, default: hi}

  - type: served_downstream
    executor: third-party
    subscribes:
      - node: okworker
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
        when: "\"third-party.served\" in payload.tags"
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          outcome: {type: string, default: ok}
          echo:    {type: string, default: ds}

  - type: refused_downstream
    executor: third-party
    subscribes:
      - node: okworker
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
        when: "\"third-party.refused\" in payload.tags"
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          outcome: {type: string, default: ok}
          echo:    {type: string, default: rd}

  - type: failfast
    executor: third-party
    error_types:
      "third-party/refused": {action: give_up}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          outcome: {type: string, default: fail}
          echo:    {type: string, default: ff}

  - type: retrier
    executor: third-party
    max_retries: 2
    error_types:
      "third-party/broken": {action: retry}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          outcome: {type: string, default: broken}
          echo:    {type: string, default: rt}

  - type: parker
    executor: third-party
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          outcome: {type: string, default: park}
          echo:    {type: string, default: pk}
```

## Settling outcomes

Read each node back through the ordinary surfaces:

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/nodes/$IID/okworker"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/admin/diagnostics/parked-nodes"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/nodes/$PARKED_NODE_ID"
```

A success outcome settles the node fresh, with the executor's own attribute
delta on the record — what the executor computed reaches the graph.

An error outcome settles the node failed.

A park outcome parks the node instead of settling it, and the node carries the
`transient/park` settling signal. An executor can suspend work rather than end
it.

## Error routing follows the declared class

The node whose policy maps `third-party/refused` to `give_up` is dispatched
exactly once and then fails. The node whose policy maps `third-party/broken` to
`retry` with `max_retries: 2` is dispatched three times — once plus its two
retries — before failing.

Retry policy is written against the executor author's own names.

## Declared tags steer subscriptions at run time

Of the two subscribers filtering on different declared tags of the same sender,
the one matching the tag the executor actually emitted runs, and the other never
fires. The declared tag set is both the vocabulary template authors may filter
on and the thing that decides which downstream node runs.
